questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose my destination due to the large amount of course choice within my field and the many researchers and project associated with my specific academic interest. I went to my destination because I wanted to learn new things relevant to my studies and later career, meet and network with new  people within my field, and experience new research environments.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The Incoming office university held an introductory seminar with all necessary administrative information, and the administrative and academic staff at my institute were very helpful whenever I had additional questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance from the Incoming office at my university, as well as the administrative and academic staff at my institute.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I signed up for housing offers from my host university by filling out a very simple form, and was lucky to get a room. There was no flexibility in the offer (you could not exchange the housing you got offered to any other university housing), which was a clear downside. I got the offer quite early, so I have no experience in looking for other types of housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The living experience was totally fine for only around five months, but as it was close to the cheapest available, the living and cleanliness standards could have been better. I had around 30 mins commute to campus, which was totally fine, although since public transport was very expensive, I would have preferred to live closer to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very simple - the registration was done simultaneously with the information meeting at the start of the exchange stay.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: General and personalized help from the Incoming office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful, and even took the opportunity to switch one of my classes out for one that was more relevant to me after the first two weeks of the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the instructions sent out in emails before the stay very closely - if you do, most things will probably go very smoothly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses varied quite a bit, however, in general, I though it was appropriate with the background I came from.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was mostly the same, seminar-based style I've experienced at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Diversity of Indo-European Languages, Methods in Evolutionary Language Science, Conditions of Language Dynamics, Written Paper in Language Diachrony and Typologies of Linguistic Structures.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Conditions of Language Dynamics, since it was very well structured and taught, and since it covers a topic (the mechanisms and nature of language change) which I've not seen courses focusing on elsewhere. I would also recommend Methods in Evolutionary Language Science to anyone who has a little bit of experience with statistical analysis beforehand (I found the level to be slightly too high, since I only had experience with qualitative methods from before), and Typologies of Linguistic Structures to anyone who would like a basic overview of linguistic typology.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Having to get extra travel tickets to get to my host country due to massive train delays.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Certain medicines were more expensive than expected. Some food, e.g. vegetables, were less expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use it personally, but there were free sports and training opportunities to sign up to via the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: See above for sports. There was a city-tour organized by the Incoming office, and other than that, social events organized by student clubs at my institution as well as academic talks for both students and staff.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to try out the sports if you're interested (probably a great place to meet people), as well as to attend both academic and social events put on by your institute or within your field of study.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around the country (especially for hiking and skiining) with the train is nice if you have the money for it (trains are very expensive). Other than that, making plans with fellow students in courses or from your housing to do things together in the city is nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to events put on by your institution or by the student clubs associated with your specific field of study. Be friendly and chat to people in your courses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The biggest difference was the use of polite pronouns to university staff - this was slightly tricky, as this is not necessarily a tradition when communicating in English, but part of the German-speaking culture in the host city.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness - in general, people were more open and chatty than is normal in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The cost of living is high, but honestly, Copenhagen is not that much cheaper.
2. Try to do any medical errands and go to the doctor in Denmark before you leave, as I've heard this can be very expensive. 
3. If you know you want to see the Alps and travel around, plan ahead - the half-fare travel card might be very worth it. Another cheaper way to travel is to join ESN's trips, which is also a great way to make friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some courses at the university are so-called "two-semester"-courses, where all of the teaching takes place in the first semester and the examination usually in the second semester. If you chose courses like this, double check with both universities (host and UCPH) that this is compatible with your one-semester exchange.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting students and academics within my field of study and hearing their different perspectives.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The reason I went on exchange was essentially only academic, so I sometimes felt demotivated to engage socially and develop friendships, as I would rather have worked on longer-term relationships in at home Copenhagen.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
